query: derive_ibata2021_stream_names.py -- nearest-track assignment by median angular separation
extraction: DERIVED, not measured. For each of the 32 published stream labels, every member star was matched to the closest point of each of the 45 galstreams v1.2.1 ibata2021 celestial tracks; the track with the smallest MEDIAN separation wins.
measurement_or_model: DERIVED NAMING AID -- NOT A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A PHYSICAL MODEL. It adds no physical information; it only attaches a probable literature name to each published integer label. Use the published integer label as the authoritative key.
note: WHY THIS EXISTS: Ibata et al. 2021 (ApJ 914, 123) publish a per-star stream label 1-32 but NO label-to-name mapping. The paper states the label is decoded only by "the different colors of the streams in the bottom panel of Figure 4"; the VizieR ReadMe likewise gives only "[1/32] A unique stream identification label; used in Figures 1-3". VALIDATION: two per-stream counts quoted in the paper text reproduce EXACTLY -- the paper says "A total of 276 stars are identified as candidate members" of the NGC 6397 stream (derived label 26 has n_stars=276) and "A total of 388 stars" for the NGC 3201 stream (derived label 9 has n_stars=388). 29 of 32 labels are assigned with median separation < 1 deg. WEAKEST assignments: label 16 (Fimbulthul, median_sep 1.045 deg, ratio only 1.2 -- AMBIGUOUS), label 28 (Gunnthra, 1.160 deg), label 11 (Slidr, 1.151 deg). Treat those three as uncertain. Totals: 5960 stars, 685 with a non-null HRV, of which 683 are credible (two published HRVs are unphysical: -3837.77 and +16856.83 km/s).
